leads.summary: Deep filtered menu results have no matching row in the unfiltered parent on Back
leads.consequence: When a root search finds a submenu multiple levels below root (for example Style > Menu Bar), activating it stores that descendant's itemId but clears the search. Back rebuilds only root's immediate children, fails to find the saved ID, and leaves the cursor on the first row (Apps), not the searched branch/row. The previous search text is also gone. A nested jump from another menu has the same shape. Consider either restoring the parent filter as part of the history frame or resolving the saved result to its nearest visible ancestor after clearing the filter.

leads.summary: Back from a directly summoned submenu still highlights its first child rather than the row just left
leads.consequence: `omarchy menu summon style.bar` opens without a history frame. Back uses the fallback branch, entering `style`, where `setActiveMenu` resets selectedIndex to zero: the shipped menu selects Theme (its first row), not Menu Bar. In the small isolated fixture with Font first, it selects Font. No frame was saved to identify the originating row. The same applies to the shipped direct submenu keybindings. A fallback should try the departed menu's own ID (or link/ancestor) in the parent display, with a selectable-row check.

leads.summary: Coordinate with the other open history-restoration PRs before merge
leads.consequence: The diverged open #12644, #13012, #12759, #7954, #11577 and #7074 all modify the same `setActiveMenu`/`goBack` history block with different frame keys or restore strategies. Git merge-file of each other head against this pinned head produces conflict markers (two conflicts per file); a resolution that keeps only one side's push/pop breaks the other's restore, and #12644's newly added tests require its own signature and `{menu,item}` frame. #12644 explicitly handles deep search ancestors and direct-route Back, which H1/H2 lack. Other diverged menu PRs #13043, #11580, and #8318 also have confirmed textual merge conflicts (respectively 10, 55, and 8 conflict hunks) in different routing/search/key-handler code, though no separate runtime defect was established for them. Pick/reconcile a single history representation and carry over the search and no-history behavior and tests, rather than accepting one conflicting block unchanged. GitHub reports the other PRs MERGEABLE against their own bases, not against #13225.

leads.summary: The unchanged menu test can pass even if the entire new restoration loop is deleted

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** Going back from a submenu now returns the cursor to the row that was entered. This holds for keyboard entry, pointer clicks, link rows and every level of a nested history. No defect was found in the change itself in the tested scope. The main thing to know is that seven other open PRs implement the same restore, and this one conflicts with all of them.

| Scenario (harness, see Test scope) | Base | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Root > Style, Back | Apps (row 0) | Style (row 3) |
| Root > Style > Menu Bar > Position, Back ×3 | Position, Theme, Apps | Position, Menu Bar, Style |
| Click Setup, Back | Apps | Setup |
| Type "style" at root, open Style, Back | Apps | Style |
| Style, Back, Setup, Back | Apps, Apps | Style, Setup |

If the entered row is hidden or no longer selectable on return, the cursor falls back to the first selectable row, as on the base.

`navStack` changes from strings to `{menuId, selectedItemId}` objects. It is read and written only inside `Menu.qml`, and is reset when the menu or dmenu opens, so no other consumer depends on the old string entries in this tree.

### Overlaps with seven open PRs for the same behaviour

#7074, #7954, #11577, #12098, #12644, #12759 and #13012 all change the same lines in `setActiveMenu` and `goBack` to restore the cursor on Back, some by numeric index and some by item id. A three-way merge of this head against each of them conflicts in `Menu.qml`. On 2026-09-21, #7657, #7800 and #8322 were closed as duplicates of #7074 with the note: "If you feel this is the wrong decision, please open the PR again with a note on the difference." This PR's description references none of the related PRs.

This PR does differ from #7074 in ways the harness shows:

| Scenario (harness) | #7074 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Type "style" at root, open Style, Back | Apps | Style |
| A row above Network in Setup is hidden while inside Network, then Back | Default (wrong row) | Network |

#7074 restores by numeric index; this PR restores by item id and skips rows that are not selectable.

**Impact:** Maintainers are likely to consolidate these into one PR. Without the comparison, the item-id restore in this PR may be closed as another duplicate.

**Suggested change:** Add the related PR numbers to the description and state the difference, for example restoring by item id, which keeps the right row after opening a direct-child search result or after rows change inside the submenu.

### Not covered: deep search results and menus opened directly into a submenu

Two Back paths still land on the first row, as on the base:

```text
Root, type "position", open Style > Menu Bar > Position, Back
  saved row: style.bar.position     (a search result, not a direct child of root)
  root rebuilt unfiltered: no row with that id  ->  Apps (row 0)

Menu opened straight into System (for example SUPER+ESCAPE), Back
  openExistingMenu() clears navStack -> goBack() parent fallback -> Apps (row 0)
```

**Impact:** After a deep search result, and after opening a menu through the shipped direct-submenu bindings (SUPER+ESCAPE for System, SUPER+CTRL+C for Capture), Back still loses the user's place. #12644 handles both cases: it falls back to the nearest visible ancestor, and it uses the menu being left as the row to select when there is no history.

**Suggested change:** Either state these limits in the description, or map the saved id to its visible ancestor row and, in the no-history fallback, select the row of the menu being left.

**Optional test improvement:** With the restore loop deleted from this head, the six menu shell tests that read the menu files still pass. Their output is byte-identical to the base, which has no restore at all. An assertion on which row is selected after Back (direct child, nested levels, missing or disabled row) would catch a regression. `docs/testing.md` and `docs/menu.md` describe keeping pure menu logic in `MenuModel.js`, where the Node tests can cover it.

**Note on #12823:** it merges cleanly with this PR, but its remembered-history filter calls `root.item(id)` on each `navStack` entry as if entries were strings. If both land, that filter would drop the object entries this PR creates. This was read from source, not run.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of `shell/plugins/menu/Menu.qml` at head `1a2df53` against base `c599d23`. Six existing menu shell tests (`menu-test.sh`, `menu-guards-test.sh`, `app-search-test.sh`, `menu-plugin-test.sh` and two others) ran in an isolated sandbox at base and head, and all passed with identical output. The scenarios above come from a Node harness that runs the functions extracted from each tree's `Menu.qml` with its own `MenuModel.js` and shipped menu file. `ListModel`, `positionViewAtIndex` and `Qt.callLater` are mocked. A copy of the head with the restore loop removed served as a control. The related PRs were compared with the same harness (#7074, #13012, #12644) and by three-way merge. Not tested: a live Quickshell session, so the on-screen highlight and real ListView scrolling were not observed.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
